reading.body:
Glean is an enterprise AI platform that connects to a company's internal data through over 100 connectors, positioning itself around information retrieval, content creation, and AI agents for automation. The company was founded in 2019 and is based in Palo Alto.

Enterprise AI adoption depends on solving a specific infrastructure problem: making proprietary company data accessible to AI systems while preserving security and access controls. Glean's emphasis on permission-aware retrieval and data access governance addresses this directly. This matters for AI scaling because most value in enterprise settings sits behind permission walls. An AI that cannot respect those boundaries is restricted to public data only, which is a far smaller training and inference surface.

The deployment list includes Booking.com, Ericsson, GCash, and Zillow. Zillow's stated 80% adoption rate suggests meaningful integration into actual workflows rather than pilot status. The broader pattern is that companies are moving past chatbot experiments toward AI that can do real work with real internal data. This is the necessary step between general-purpose AI and actual business value.

The data does not cover Glean's infrastructure footprint, compute requirements, power consumption, or data center strategy. It does not explain what data volume these deployments actually handle or whether scale has hit any constraints on retrieval speed or governance overhead. California legal exposure is noted at 181 cases but no details are provided on their nature or significance.

profile_text.body:
Glean is a for-profit startup founded in 2019 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Its website describes the company as an enterprise AI platform connected to an enterprise's data, with the stated goal of letting users find, create, and automate anything. The site says the platform is built for enterprise from day one and that answers are secure, explainable, and permission-aware. Customer examples on the site include Booking.com, Ericsson, GCash, and Zillow; a Zillow quote on the site reports an 80% adoption rate of Glean.

The company's product is listed in the enterprise AI platforms and agent orchestration category as enterprise knowledge search AI with 100+ connectors, permission-aware retrieval, and data access governance. The site names platform components including Glean Enterprise Context Connectors and Actions APIs, API Lookbook, Glean Protect, Glean Intelligence, Auto routing, Model hub, Usage controls, and AI Gateway. A Model Context Protocol server named co.gleanit/gleanit is listed for searching, reading, and writing highlights, notes, screenshots, collections, projects, and tags in Gleanit.

The company has 281 law exposure entries in California and no listed litigation cases.
